tokenizer.name: o200k_base
tokenizer.counted_text: each output file exactly as stored, decoded as UTF-8 (no normalization; line endings and any BOM are kept)
tokenizer.special_tokens: strings such as '<|endoftext|>' are counted as ordinary text: countTokens(text, { disallowedSpecial: new Set() }), like tiktoken's disallowed_special=()

steps: 1. Unicode NFKC: text.normalize('NFKC') (ligatures, full-width forms and no-break spaces become plain characters)
2. Case-insensitive: String.prototype.toLowerCase() (locale-independent Unicode default lowercase mapping)
3. Markdown emphasis and escape characters are deleted: every '*', '_', '\' and '`'
4. Table pipes: every '|' becomes a space, so '|a|b|' and '| a | b |' both read 'a b'
5. NFKC again, so a deletion cannot leave an unnormalized sequence (e.g. 'e', '*', combining acute)
6. Whitespace: every run of JavaScript \s characters (Unicode White_Space incl. line breaks, tabs, NBSP, U+FEFF) becomes one space; the ends are trimmed
normalization.applied_to: the candidate output and every ground-truth string (must_contain phrases, ordered anchors, headings, table cells, noise texts, absent strings) before they are compared
normalization.text_and_order_only: after steps 1-6, for must_contain phrases and ordered anchors (on both sides) a hyphen-minus between a letter or digit and a letter loses the space that follows it: /([\p{L}\p{N}])- (?=\p{L})/gu -> '$1-', so a compound broken at a line end ('per-' + line break + 'pound', '40,000-' + line break + 'pound') reads 'per-pound', '40,000-pound'. A split word ('regu-' + line break + 'lation') becomes 'regu-lation', which still differs from 'regulation'. Not applied to headings, table cells, noise or absent strings.
normalization.table_cells_only: after steps 1-6, a table cell (expected or parsed) that is a number written with comma thousands separators loses those commas: the whole cell must match /^(?:[a-z]{3} ?)?[(+\-\u2212]?[$€£¥]?[(+\-\u2212]?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?%?\)?\.?$/u (optional three-letter currency code, sign, parenthesis and currency symbol; groups of exactly 3 digits; optional decimals, '%', ')' and a final '.'); signs, decimals, currency and parentheses are kept, so '1,849,906' = '1849906' and '$7,560.00' = '$7560.00' but '$7,560.00' != '7560'.
normalization.matching: must_contain, ordered and noise match as substrings of the normalized output (no word-boundary rule); absent strings use the word-boundary and split-word rule of absent_violations; table cells must be equal after normalization
normalization.not_unified:
nothing else is unified: curly vs straight quotes, dash and hyphen variants, soft hyphens (U+00AD), zero-width characters, HTML entities,
and CSV's doubled quotes outside parsed CSV tables stay distinct; other Markdown syntax ('#', '-', '>', list numbers, link brackets) stays in the text

metric_definitions.text_recall: found / total over checks.must_contain; a phrase is found when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized output, both normalized with the compound-hyphen rule (normalization.text_and_order_only). null when must_contain is empty.
metric_definitions.order_score: Each anchor's position is the first occurrence of its normalized text in the normalized output (both with the compound-hyphen rule of normalization.text_and_order_only). order_score = length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of the positions of the anchors that were found, taken in ground-truth order, divided by the number of anchors; a missing anchor counts as not in order. not_in_order lists the found anchors outside one such longest subsequence (when several tie, the one patience sorting reconstructs, which ends at the smallest position; ties never change the score). null when ordered is empty.
metric_definitions.heading_recall: Heading lines are CommonMark ATX headings outside fenced code blocks: up to 3 spaces of indentation, 1-6 '#', then a space, a tab or the end of the line; an optional closing run of '#' is dropped. Setext (underlined) headings, bold lines and HTML headings do not count. An expected heading is found when its normalized text is a substring of the normalized text of a heading line; each heading line can satisfy at most one expected heading (maximum one-to-one matching). heading_recall = found / total; null when headings is empty.
metric_definitions.table_recall: The headline table metric. Pipe tables are parsed like GFM tables, outside fenced code blocks: a header line followed by a delimiter line (cells of the form :?-+:?, at least one unescaped '|', the same cell count as the header line), then body lines until a blank line, a line without an unescaped '|', an ATX heading or a code fence (one deliberate difference from GFM: a non-blank line without a '|' right after a table ends it instead of becoming a one-cell row); body rows are padded with empty cells or cut to the header width; '\|' does not split cells. CSV blocks are parsed as tables too (RFC 4180: comma-separated, a field holding a comma, quote or line break is quoted, a doubled quote inside quotes is one quote): (1) a fenced code block whose info string starts with 'csv', with at least 2 records and a header of at least 2 fields (rows padded or cut to the header width; a block with an unterminated quote or a stray quote is not a table); (2) outside code fences, a paragraph (a run of non-blank lines that are not ATX headings, fences or pipe-table lines) whose lines, after at most one leading caption line, are all one-line CSV records with the same field count of at least 2, at least 2 records in all; a record must not start with a Markdown block marker ('>', '- ', '* ', '+ ', '1. ', '1) '), and no unquoted field may start or end with whitespace (so prose with ', ' never qualifies). The caption line is not part of the table. Parsed tables of both kinds are used in document order. Cells are compared after normalization.table_cells_only (comma thousands separators dropped from whole-cell numbers on both sides). A column of a parsed table that is empty in every row, header included, is padding: each parsed table is scored as written and again with such columns dropped, and the variant with more matching cells is kept (as written on a tie); column indices reported always refer to the table as written. For each expected table, every parsed table is scored: (a) columns are paired by equal non-empty normalized header text, one-to-one, left to right; (b) each other expected column is paired by position, keeping the column offset of the nearest header-paired column (looking left first, then right; offset 0 when no column was paired by header), if that column exists and is free; (c) expected columns still unpaired take the remaining free columns left to right; (d) rows, header rows included, are aligned in order by dynamic programming to maximize the number of matching cells. A matching cell is an aligned pair of cells with equal, non-empty normalized text; an aligned row pair whose only matching cell is a number (a cell without a letter) does not count, unless it is the only non-empty cell of the expected row (a lone shared '5' or '2024', such as a table-of-contents page number, is no evidence that two rows correspond; a lone row label such as 'Bob' still counts). Cells that are empty after normalization are not counted on either side. recall R = matching cells / non-empty expected cells; precision P = matching cells / non-empty cells of the parsed table; F1 = 2PR / (P + R), 0 when P + R = 0. Separately for each expected table, the parsed table with the highest recall is picked; ties on recall go to the higher precision, then to the earliest table in the output. A parsed table with no matching cell is never picked: when no parsed table has a matching cell (or the output has none), R = P = F1 = 0 and no table is named. table_recall = mean R over expected tables. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.table_precision: Secondary. Mean P over expected tables, each P taken from the same parsed table that table_recall picked. Precision is secondary because an expected table can be partial: it may list only some rows of a larger source table, so a complete, faithful conversion carries correct cells beyond the expected ones, and they lower precision. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.table_f1: Secondary. Mean F1 over expected tables, each F1 computed on the same parsed table that table_recall picked (so it is not the best F1 over all parsed tables). Secondary for the same reason as table_precision. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.spurious_table_cells: Secondary; does not change table_recall. The number of non-empty cells inside parsed tables (pipe and CSV) that sit on no ground-truth table cell. Every parsed table is aligned with every expected table by the table_recall rules (column pairing, empty-column variant, row alignment; a row pair is aligned only when it has matching cells that count under rule (d)). A parsed cell sits on a ground-truth cell when, for at least one expected table, its row is aligned to an expected row, its column is paired with an expected column and that expected cell is non-empty; such a cell is not spurious even when its text differs (a wrong value lowers recall and precision instead). Everything else counts: tables built from prose, rows no expected row aligns with (titles, captions, stray text), placeholder header cells ('Column 2', 'Unnamed: 1') and filler such as 'NaN' where the expected cell is empty. Rows of a real table that the ground truth does not list also count, so compare tools on the same file. tables.per_output_table gives the figure for each parsed table. null when tables is empty.
metric_definitions.noise_excess: For each noise entry, count the non-overlapping occurrences of its normalized text in the normalized output; excess = max(0, count - max). noise_excess = sum of the excesses. null when noise is empty.
metric_definitions.absent_violations: Number of absent entries present in the output (each entry counts once). Entry and output are normalized (steps 1-6, no compound-hyphen rule). An entry is present when (a) its normalized text occurs in the normalized output and, if it starts with a letter or digit, the occurrence does not start inside a word (no letter or digit right before it); or (b) the entry is a split word '<prefix>- <rest>' (prefix ending in a letter or digit, rest starting with a letter) and the output, read line by line (each line normalized, blank lines skipped), has '<prefix>-' starting a word and followed by a space or the end of the line, with '<rest>' starting a word later on that line or on one of the next 2 lines. Rule (b) catches a line-end hyphen whose two halves were pulled apart by text from another column; absent.found_split lists the entries found only that way. null when absent is empty.
metric_definitions.size: chars = Unicode code points of the output file as stored; bytes = its UTF-8 bytes; tokens = o200k_base tokens of the same text (see tokenizer). A missing output is empty: 0 / 0 / 0.
metric_definitions.aggregates: Macro averages: for each candidate, the mean of each per-file score over the files where that check applies (n). Missing outputs are scored as empty text and included. For tables, table_recall is the headline number (the tblRec column of the stderr summary); table_precision and table_f1 are kept beside it as secondary fields. spurious_table_cells (the spur column), noise_excess and absent_violations give their total and mean per file; chars and tokens give totals and means. complete_files = files where every candidate produced an output; tokens.total_on_complete_files sums tokens over those files only, and tokens.ratio_vs_markitdown_on_complete_files divides it by markitdown's sum on the same files.
metric_definitions.rounding: Non-integer numbers in the report are rounded to 6 decimal places when written; means are computed from unrounded values.
